articles.title: Building a Zapier Integration for a Tiny SaaS: The API Key Default I Almost Shipped
articles.excerpt: I run a small SaaS that puts an AI assistant on small business websites. It answers visitors and captures leads. Owners kept asking the same thing: "Can the leads go straight into my CRM / Google Shee…
articles.body: I run a small SaaS that puts an AI assistant on small business websites. It answers visitors and captures leads. Owners kept asking the same thing: "Can the leads go straight into my CRM / Google Sheet / Slack?" The answer to "connect to everything" is usually Zapier, so I built a public Zapier integration. It took an afternoon to get working and most of a day to get right. This post is about the gap between those two, including one default that would have leaked every customer's API key into URLs. The API surface: two endpoints Zapier's polling triggers need surprisingly little from you: An endpoint to test the connection , so Zapier can confirm a key is valid when a user connects. An endpoint that returns recent items as an array , newest first.
articles.author: Mohsin Azam

articles.title: Node.js Presigned URL Audit for Backup Downloads (Object Storage Retention)
articles.excerpt: A selected backup snapshot should remain private until an authorized tenant asks to restore it. The least complex way to deliver its archive is a short-lived presigned download URL for one object, iss…
articles.body: A selected backup snapshot should remain private until an authorized tenant asks to restore it. The least complex way to deliver its archive is a short-lived presigned download URL for one object, issued after a tenant-scoped lookup. The deletion timer belongs to the snapshot record, not to the link. TL;DR: treat a presigned URL as a bearer credential, not delivery proof. Keep the backup object private, authorize the snapshot before signing, record issuance without recording the URL, and alert only when a restore is stalled past evidence you can trust. For an e-commerce system, this matters after the order database or a tenant configuration has to be rolled back to one selected snapshot. A predictable object key is convenient during an incident.

That's a division of labor many freelancers settle on. One caveat up front: this is today's answer. All three get new models every few months, and the split has to be reshuffled from time to time. A simple experiment makes the differences obvious: before a deadline, have all three revise the same paragraph and compare the results. The content is accurate in every version, but the editing habits are clearly different.

articles.title: A Traditional Switch Does Not Care Which Wire Is Which; a Smart Switch Does
articles.excerpt: A wall switch from 1965 is a piece of metal that either touches or does not. If you swap the two wires on its terminals, nothing changes, because electricity flowing through a contact does not care ab…
articles.body: A wall switch from 1965 is a piece of metal that either touches or does not. If you swap the two wires on its terminals, nothing changes, because electricity flowing through a contact does not care about direction. That freedom is gone the moment you replace the metal with a small computer. A smart switch has a logic board, a power supply stage, and a relay, and each of those parts has a defined place in the circuit. The two terminals on the old switch were interchangeable. The four or five terminals on the new one are not, and the difference shows up in ways most installation guides never explain. Why the Old Switch Never Cared A mechanical switch sits in series with the lamp.

articles.title: Stop Uploading Your Photos to Random Websites Just to Resize Them

articles.body: Ever needed to quickly compress a screenshot before attaching it to a Jira ticket, or convert a WebP file your design tool spat out into something Word actually accepts? Most of us have, and the usual flow goes: search for "online image compressor", pick one of the first results, and upload your image to some server you know nothing about. That last step always bothered me. Half the time the image is something mundane — a screenshot, a chart, a photo for a slide deck. But sometimes it's something more personal, like a scan of a document or a photo of your family. And you're trusting an anonymous website to handle it. That's why I was glad to come across PicShik . It's a free image toolkit that runs entirely in your browser.

articles.title: You don't have to go to the moon to see Earth differently: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover on what really matters
articles.excerpt: After a record-breaking journey around the moon, Artemis 2 astronaut Victor Glover explains why you don't need to travel into space to see Earth differently.
articles.body: TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Imagine traveling over 250 million miles from home, watching Earth disappear behind the moon and losing contact with the billions of people who call it home. What would you miss most? For Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover, the answer wasn't a particular place, a familiar view or even the comforts of home. It was something much more fundamental: human connection. Speaking during a discussion with former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival on Oct. 18 in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Glover reflected on the extraordinary experience of traveling around the moon and how being so far from Earth had given him a renewed appreciation for the people living on it. "The greatest reason to go to space, it isn't to be a swashbuckler hero," Glover said.

articles.excerpt: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is back in communication after the 49-year-old spacecraft briefly fell silent last month, during its interstellar-space mission.
articles.body: Voyager, 1, humanity's most distant spacecraft, is back in contact after briefly losing touch with Earth last month. The spacecraft stopped phoning home for about 48 hours between Oct. 18 and 20 due to a communications glitch that Voyager 1 resolved on its own, before engineers could send the long-running spacecraft a remote fix. "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said in an agency statement about the incident on Oct. 29.
